findings.note: The capture loop validates source paths but never validates manifest destinations or expanded destination collisions (unlike speckit_bootstrap.py:_collect_bundle, lines 118-159). Invalid/colliding destinations can therefore be inventoried and assembled with a completion marker although the packaged installer cannot safely consume them. Validate destination paths/collision keys before assembly and test a collision fixture.

Both verification walks call os.walk without onerror handling; it silently ignores traversal errors by default. An unreadable directory containing unlisted files can evade the required two-directional check and the verifier may report intact. Fail closed on walk errors and cover an inaccessible subtree in tests, including the assembly verification walk.

Required quickstart/manual acceptance tasks remain unchecked: real-tree assembly/refusals and offline verification; consumer install/conflict/defaults; update behavior; human docs review; boundary and scanner positive-control sweeps; traceability closure. Fixture tests do not establish these real-deliverable boundaries. Record outcomes or explicitly defer them before claiming end-to-end acceptance.
